container.title: Application / Docker Container
container.summary: Lightweight, standalone execution environment packaging application code, libraries, runtime, and configuration.
container.details: Containers encapsulate the microservice application so it runs consistently across local development, staging, and Google Cloud production environments. In this architecture, containers run your core backend API and background tasks.
container.architectureRole: Packaged as a Docker image, pushed to Google Artifact Registry, and orchestrated across servers using Google Cloud Run.

ecr.title: Google Artifact Registry
ecr.summary: Fully managed, secure container image and language package registry on Google Cloud.
ecr.details:
Artifact Registry is the evolution of Container Registry (GCR), providing encrypted storage, vulnerability scanning, and IAM access controls.

• Best for: Version controlling application container builds and securely delivering them to Cloud Run, GKE, and Compute Engine.
• The Catch: It is strictly storage; pushing an image does nothing until a compute service like Cloud Run pulls and executes it.
ecr.architectureRole: Receives container builds from CI/CD and acts as the secure source repository from which Cloud Run pulls images.

ecs.title: Google Cloud Run
ecs.summary: Fully managed serverless compute platform that enables you to run containers directly on top of Google's scalable infrastructure.
ecs.details:
Cloud Run abstracts away all infrastructure management and automatically scales containers from zero to thousands of instances.

Key Launch Configurations:
1. Cloud Run Services: Responds to incoming HTTPS web requests, automatically scaling based on concurrent requests.
2. Cloud Run Jobs: Executes batch processes or long-running operational tasks that run to completion without serving web traffic.
ecs.architectureRole: Executes backend container tasks behind the Cloud Load Balancer and interacts with Cloud SQL, Memorystore, and Cloud Tasks.

rds.title: Google Cloud SQL / AlloyDB
rds.summary: Fully managed relational database service supporting PostgreSQL, MySQL, and SQL Server.
rds.details: Automates database provisioning, automated storage increases, automated backups, point-in-time recovery, security patching, and multi-zone high availability with automated failover.
rds.architectureRole: Stores relational structured application data, queried directly by Cloud Run containers and Cloud Functions.

sqs.title: Google Cloud Tasks
sqs.summary: Fully managed task queue service managing the execution, dispatch, and delivery of a large number of distributed tasks.
sqs.details:
Cloud Tasks handles asynchronous dispatching with granular rate-limiting, retry configurations, and deduplication.

• Decoupled Task Execution: Dispatches discrete units of work to Cloud Run or Cloud Functions with guaranteed delivery.
• Retry & Rate Limiting: Controls maximum dispatch rates to avoid overwhelming downstream services.
sqs.architectureRole: Buffers background and long-running requests from Cloud Run to be consumed asynchronously by worker Cloud Functions.

lambda.title: Google Cloud Functions
lambda.summary: Scalable, pay-as-you-go serverless execution environment for building event-driven applications.
lambda.details:
Cloud Functions runs backend code in response to events and HTTP triggers with zero server management.

In this architecture, Functions serve two core roles:
1. Event-driven post-processing (triggered automatically by Cloud Storage when a user uploads an object).
2. Asynchronous task execution consuming tasks from Cloud Tasks for jobs taking 5–15 minutes.
lambda.architectureRole: Triggered by Cloud Storage upload events and Cloud Tasks queue items to process data and push notifications.

ses.title: SendGrid on GCP / Google Workspace SMTP
ses.summary: Managed cloud-based email delivery service providing high inbox placement for transactional emails.
ses.details: Provides reliable transactional email dispatch with custom domain authentication, SPF/DKIM verification, delivery analytics, and bounce handling.
ses.architectureRole: Dispatched by worker Cloud Functions to send task completion emails, account confirmations, and transactional receipts.

elasticache.title: Google Cloud Memorystore (Redis)
elasticache.summary: Fully managed in-memory data store service for Redis and Memcached providing sub-millisecond latency.
elasticache.details: Dramatically accelerates application responsiveness and reduces database load by caching hot data, session states, rate limits, and real-time leaderboards.
elasticache.architectureRole: Caches hot data for Cloud Run and Cloud Functions to offload repetitive read queries from Cloud SQL.

sns.title: Google Cloud Pub/Sub (Topics)
sns.summary: Globally distributed, asynchronous messaging service that decouples services producing events from services processing events.
sns.details: Publishers push messages to a topic, and Pub/Sub delivers them to multiple fan-out subscribers (Cloud Functions, Cloud Run, Cloud Tasks) with automatic scaling.
sns.architectureRole: Fans out system status changes and operational events to multiple backend consumers and notification webhooks.

elasticache_sns.title: In-Memory Cache & Pub/Sub (Memorystore / Cloud Pub/Sub)
elasticache_sns.summary: Combined caching and event distribution cluster managing state speed and real-time event dissemination.
elasticache_sns.details: This composite cluster pairs sub-millisecond caching via Cloud Memorystore (Redis) with global asynchronous event distribution via Cloud Pub/Sub.
elasticache_sns.architectureRole: Provides caching for database query offloading alongside pub/sub event broadcasting for internal microservices.

cloudfront.title: Google Cloud CDN
cloudfront.summary: High-performance, global Content Delivery Network leveraging Google's private fiber network.
cloudfront.details: Caches static assets and media close to users at hundreds of edge Points of Presence (PoPs) worldwide, reducing latency, terminating TLS at the edge, and offloading origin servers.
cloudfront.architectureRole: Distributes static web frontend assets cached from Google Cloud Storage and proxies dynamic API traffic toward the Cloud Load Balancer.

s3.title: Google Cloud Storage (GCS)
s3.summary: Worldwide, durable, and highly scalable object storage designed for 99.999999999% (11 9's) annual durability.
s3.details:
Stores unstructured data, images, videos, backups, and static website assets.

• Signed URLs: Enables clients to securely upload directly (Signed URL POST/PUT) or download (Signed URL GET) without routing heavy payloads through application servers.
s3.architectureRole: Stores user file uploads directly via Signed URLs and triggers worker Cloud Functions automatically upon file landing.

cloudwatch.title: Google Cloud Operations Suite (Monitoring & Logging)
cloudwatch.summary: Full-stack monitoring, logging, and application performance management solution (formerly Stackdriver).
cloudwatch.details: Aggregates logs and metrics from Cloud Run, Cloud Functions, Cloud SQL, and Load Balancers. Generates metric-based alert policies and powers real-time dashboards.
cloudwatch.architectureRole: Monitors health metrics across all infrastructure and collects container & serverless logs for debugging and auditing.

route53.title: Google Cloud DNS
route53.summary: Scalable, reliable, and managed authoritative Domain Name System (DNS) service running on Google's infrastructure.
route53.details: Provides 100% availability SLA with anycast name servers distributed globally. Maps user domain names to Cloud CDN and Cloud Load Balancers with ultra-low latency.
route53.architectureRole: Top-level DNS resolving user domain queries and pointing directly to Cloud CDN edge distribution.

acm.title: Google Cloud Certificate Manager
acm.summary: Service that provisions, verifies, and automatically renews public and private SSL/TLS certificates.
acm.details: Provides free Google-managed SSL/TLS certificates for Cloud Load Balancers and Cloud CDN with zero-touch automatic DNS authorization and lifecycle renewal.
acm.architectureRole: Secures all inbound HTTPS connections by binding validated TLS certificates to Cloud CDN and Cloud Load Balancers.

elb.title: Google Cloud Network Load Balancer (Layer 4)
elb.summary: High-performance, pass-through Layer 4 load balancer for TCP/UDP traffic.
elb.details: Delivers millions of requests per second without needing pre-warming, routing network traffic across backend instances or serverless endpoints.
elb.architectureRole: Distributes incoming traffic across backend infrastructure and internal microservice endpoints.

alb.title: Google Cloud Application Load Balancer (Global HTTPS LB)
alb.summary: Global, proxy-based Layer 7 load balancer distributing HTTP/HTTPS traffic across backend services worldwide.
alb.details: Provides single global Anycast Any-IP, URL map path-based routing, Cloud Armor DDoS protection, SSL termination, and seamless integration with Serverless NEGs (Network Endpoint Groups) for Cloud Run.
alb.architectureRole: Receives decrypted traffic from Cloud CDN and routes REST API requests to healthy Cloud Run container services.

elb_alb.title: Cloud Load Balancing (External Application / Network LB)
elb_alb.summary: Global load balancing infrastructure routing external user requests to serverless container workloads.
elb_alb.details: Combines Global External Application Load Balancer for Layer 7 path routing and SSL termination with Serverless Network Endpoint Groups for zero-downtime scaling.
elb_alb.architectureRole: Acts as the single entry point for API traffic reaching the backend container infrastructure.

iam.title: Google Cloud IAM (Identity and Access Management)
iam.summary: Fine-grained access control and identity management governing authorizations across Google Cloud resources.
iam.details: Enforces least-privilege permissions using Service Accounts with temporary credentials, avoiding hard-coded API keys in application source code.
iam.architectureRole: Grants granular permissions allowing Cloud Run containers and Cloud Functions to securely access Cloud Storage, SQL, and Tasks.

parameter_store.title: Google Cloud Secret Manager
parameter_store.summary: Secure and convenient storage system for API keys, passwords, database credentials, and certificates.
parameter_store.details: Provides centralized, versioned, encrypted storage for sensitive data with fine-grained Cloud IAM access control and audit logging.
parameter_store.architectureRole: Supplies encrypted database passwords and API configuration keys to containers and Cloud Functions on startup.

opensearch.title: Google Cloud Vertex AI Search / Elasticsearch
opensearch.summary: Fully managed enterprise search and analytics engine with keyword, vector, and semantic search capabilities.
opensearch.details: Enables sub-second search queries across large catalogs with autocomplete, fuzzy matching, faceted filtering, generative summaries, and vector similarity search.
opensearch.architectureRole: Powers high-speed application search queries and real-time faceted exploration alongside primary relational data.

api_gateway.title: Google Cloud Run (WebSockets) / API Gateway
api_gateway.summary: Fully managed API and real-time streaming endpoint supporting bidirectional WebSocket connections.
api_gateway.details:
Maintains persistent, stateful WebSocket connections with client applications.

When long-running asynchronous tasks (5–15 minutes) complete, backend worker Functions broadcast live notifications directly back to users without requiring client polling.
api_gateway.architectureRole: Maintains active WebSocket links with clients to push notifications when asynchronous tasks finish.

cloudflare.title: Cloudflare
cloudflare.summary: Global CDN, DNS, and DDoS protection layer positioned at the Internet perimeter before Google Cloud origins.
cloudflare.details: Provides edge caching, Web Application Firewall (WAF) rule sets, bot management, and SSL termination before routing legitimate traffic to Google Cloud CDN or Cloud DNS.
cloudflare.architectureRole: Acts as the outermost internet security shield and DNS proxy guarding the architecture against malicious traffic.

user.title: End User / Web Client
user.summary: End-user web browser or mobile client initiating HTTP requests, WebSocket streams, and file transfers.
user.details: Clients fetch static assets from Cloud CDN, connect to Cloud Run via WebSockets for real-time progress updates, and upload files directly to Google Cloud Storage via Signed URLs without loading application servers.
user.architectureRole: Interacts with Cloud CDN for assets, Cloud Run for live WebSocket alerts, and Cloud Storage for direct uploads.

admin.title: Administrator Client
admin.summary: System administrator or staff member accessing administrative panels, metrics dashboards, and configuration tools.
admin.details: Admins access operational views, monitor Cloud Monitoring metrics, inspect Vertex Search analytics, and manage application secrets stored in Secret Manager.
admin.architectureRole: Consumes administrative APIs and observability dashboards to monitor system health and perform operational duties.
